correctness.rationale: For every a,b>=2 the graph has a+b+1 edges and a+b vertices, with spanning trees obtained by omitting exactly one edge on each of two different terminal paths. This gives W(z)=Sigma[XY+delta(X+Y)] with all sign conventions specified. The finite-group Fourier projection convolution kernel is W/2^(a+b+1) and has exactly the endpoint l1 norms given by the average absolute W. Averaging direct-edge sign yields max(|XY|,|X+Y|). The integer identity for its difference from |XY| is verified case by case, and exact Rademacher binomial probabilities give the displayed formula for all a,b. Solving (X+delta)(Y+delta)=1 for integers yields precisely the stated Fourier-zero multiplicities. Stirling expansion gives both equal-length parity limits. The independent graph/tree enumerator and integer Walsh-Hadamard checker has been run on 24 instances a,b=2..6 with a+b<=11. These finite checks are corroborative, not the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The Fourier Lebesgue constant for all spanning-tree incidence vectors is a natural sharp harmonic invariant of the first simple noncactus bicyclic theta family. Its exact two-parameter norm is not a routine tree-count or coefficient evaluation: the new piece is a nonlinear absolute Walsh average, simplified to explicit central-binomial probabilities. Exact kernel-zero multiplicity and the different constants in even/odd long-path asymptotics describe genuine interacting-cycle structure. This is a complete natural infinite-family classification with plausible use as an exactly solvable benchmark for spectral amplification on graphic-matroid bases.
